questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.text: From which of the following countries Giuseppe Garibaldi belonged to ?
questions.solution: Garibaldi was an Italian revolutionary who led the Red Shirts in the unification of Italy.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Which one of the following pairs regarding Indian nationalism is correctly matched ? (Leader : Contribution)
options: Sardar Patel : Hindustan Socialist Republican Army
Jawahar Lal Nehru : Oudh Kisan Sabha
questions.solution: The Oudh Kisan Sabha was set up in 1920 by Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramchandra and others. (Patel led the Bardoli Satyagraha, Bhagat Singh was in the HSRA, and C.R. Das formed the Swaraj Party.)

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Choose the correctly matched pair.
questions.solution: Limestone is a non-metallic mineral. Nickel and cobalt are ferrous metallic minerals, and natural gas is an energy mineral.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Read the given statements and choose the correct option with regard to Rabi cropping season :
I. Rabi crops are sown in winter.
II. Sown from October to December and harvested from April to June.
III. Important crops are Maize, Cotton, Jute.
IV. Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh are important for the production of wheat.
questions.solution: Statements I, II and IV describe the rabi season. Maize, cotton and jute are kharif crops.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Identify the soil with the help of following information :
• It develops in areas with high temperature.
• It is the result of intense leaching due to heavy rain.
• Humus content is low.
questions.solution: Laterite soil develops in hot areas with heavy rainfall, which causes intense leaching, and it has little humus.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Political Science: Gender, Religion and Caste
questions.text: Which of the following term refers to the belief in and advocacy for the social, political and economic equality of women ?
questions.solution: Feminists are people who believe in and work for equal rights and opportunities for women and men.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Political Science: Gender, Religion and Caste
questions.text:
Read the given statements :
• India has no official religion.
• All the communities have freedom to profess and practice any religion in India.
Which one of the following constitutional term is used for the above statements ?
questions.solution: A secular state has no official religion and gives everyone freedom to follow any religion.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Match Column I (List) with Column II (Jurisdiction Sphere) :
I. Union list subjects
II. State list subjects
III. Concurrent subjects
IV. Residuary subjects
A. State Governments alone make laws on it.
B. For uniformity Central Government legislates on it.
C. Subjects under jurisdiction of Centre and State Governments.
D. Central Government legislates on new subjects.
questions.solution: Union List: the Centre legislates for uniformity (B). State List: only states (A). Concurrent List: both (C). Residuary subjects: the Centre (D).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Which of the following was the primary objective of Belgium to form the separate government in Brussels ?
questions.solution: Brussels has a separate government with equal representation of Dutch- and French-speaking communities, to accommodate both language groups.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Which one of the following countries has two-party system ?
questions.solution: The United Kingdom (and the USA) have two-party systems. China has a one-party system and India a multiparty system.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What role do 'checks and balances' play in a democratic country ? Choose the most suitable option from the following.
options: To establish a direct form of government without representatives.
To create a separation of powers to prevent from authoritarianism.
To prevent any change to the Constitution.
To ensure absolute power for one branch of government.
questions.solution: Separating power among the legislature, executive and judiciary lets each check the others, so no organ can wield unlimited power.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Suppose, the monthly income of the family members is as follows respectively : Mother – Rs. 50,000/-, Father – Rs. 40,000/-, Son – Rs. 20,000/-, Daughter – Rs. 20,000/-. The average income of the family would be :

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Which one of the following indices is given priority by the World Bank with respect to development ?
questions.solution: The World Development Report of the World Bank classifies countries by per capita income.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Globalisation and the Indian Economy
questions.text: Removing barriers or restrictions on business and trade set by the government is called as ______.
questions.solution: Removing government barriers and restrictions is called liberalisation.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Sectors of the Indian Economy
questions.text: Which one of the following is an example of organized sector activities ?
options: A handloom weaver working in her house.
A teacher taking classes in a government school.
questions.solution: A government school teacher has regular employment with fixed terms, registered with the government, which is organised-sector work.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Which of the following are developmental goals of a prosperous farmer ? Choose the correct from the given options.
I. Better wages
II. Higher support prices for crops
III. Assured high family income
IV. More days for work
options: Only I and II are correct.
Only II and IV are correct.
Only II and III are correct.
Only I and IV are correct.
questions.solution: A prosperous farmer wants higher support prices and an assured high family income. Better wages and more days of work are goals of landless labourers.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Why do lenders often require collateral before lending loan ? Choose the most suitable option from the following.
options: To lower interest rates for borrowers.
To mitigate the risk of loan default.
questions.solution: Collateral is a guarantee: if the borrower fails to repay, the lender can sell it to recover the loan.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Which one of the following supervise the functioning of formal sources of loan in India ?
questions.solution: The Reserve Bank of India supervises the functioning of formal sources of loans.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: The Making of a Global World
questions.text: "The Silk route was a good example of vibrant pre-modern trade and cultural links between distant parts of the world." Explain the statement with any two examples.
questions.solution: Chinese silk was carried west along these routes, and textiles and spices from India and Southeast Asia travelled in return, while precious metals such as gold and silver flowed from Europe to Asia. Traders, Christian missionaries and Muslim preachers travelled the routes, and Buddhism spread from eastern India in several directions along them, linking cultures as well as economies.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Suggest any two measures for the conservation of forest.
questions.solution: Any two: afforestation and planting more trees; stopping illegal felling and controlling grazing; involving local communities in forest protection (Joint Forest Management); declaring reserved and protected forests; using alternatives to wood for fuel.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Suggest any two measures for the conservation of wildlife.
questions.solution: Any two: setting up national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves; banning hunting and trade in wildlife (Wildlife Protection Act, 1972); special projects for endangered species such as Project Tiger; spreading awareness and involving local communities.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Why is power sharing desirable ? Explain.
questions.solution: Prudential reason: it reduces the possibility of conflict between social groups and so keeps the political order stable. Moral reason: it is the very spirit of democracy; people affected by policies have a right to be consulted and to have a share in power, which makes the government legitimate.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Sectors of the Indian Economy
questions.text: Differentiate between Public and Private Sector.
questions.solution: Public sector: the government owns most of the assets and provides the services; the aim is public welfare. Example: Indian Railways. Private sector: assets are owned and services provided by private individuals or companies; the aim is profit. Example: Reliance Industries.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Describe any three causes that led to the Non-Cooperation Movement.
questions.solution: 1. The Rowlatt Act (1919), which allowed detention without trial, and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre that followed. 2. The Khilafat issue: the harsh peace treaty imposed on the Ottoman emperor (the Khalifa) after the First World War, which united Hindus and Muslims. 3. Economic hardship after the war, such as rising prices, forced recruitment and crop failures, along with Gandhiji's belief that British rule survived only through Indian cooperation.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Describe any three causes of 'Civil Disobedience Movement.'
questions.solution: 1. The Simon Commission (1928) had no Indian member, which angered Indians. 2. The Lahore Congress (1929) adopted Purna Swaraj, and the Viceroy's vague offer of dominion status did not satisfy nationalists. 3. The economic depression hit peasants hard, and Gandhiji's eleven demands, including abolition of the salt tax, were rejected by Lord Irwin, leading to the Salt March in 1930.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: 'Manufacturing industries are considered the backbone of economic development.' Justify the statement.
questions.solution: Manufacturing modernises agriculture by supplying machines and inputs; it reduces dependence on agriculture by creating jobs in the secondary and tertiary sectors, helping remove unemployment and poverty; exports of manufactured goods expand trade and earn foreign exchange; and industries in backward areas reduce regional disparities.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Analyse the role of political parties in a democracy.
questions.solution: Parties contest elections and offer policies and programmes for voters to choose from; they play a decisive role in making laws; parties that win form and run governments; those that lose act as the opposition and criticise the government; they shape public opinion; and they give people access to government machinery and welfare schemes.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: How is credit essential for economic activities ? Explain with examples.
questions.solution: Credit lets people meet the costs of production before they earn income. For example, a shoe manufacturer such as Salim takes credit to buy raw materials and pay workers for a large order, and repays when the buyer pays; a farmer borrows for seeds, fertilisers and pesticides before the harvest. Credit helps raise production, earnings and employment, provided the borrower can repay (otherwise it can push people into a debt trap).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: How is the issue of sustainability important for development ? Explain.
questions.solution: Development must not harm the ability of future generations to meet their needs. Resources such as groundwater and minerals are limited: overuse of groundwater is lowering water tables, and minerals and crude oil will run out if used carelessly. Environmental damage does not respect national borders, so sustainability is everyone's concern. Present development should use resources wisely so that growth can continue in the future.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.text: How did the ideology of 'liberalism' affect the Europe in early nineteenth century ? Explain.
questions.solution: Liberalism (from the Latin liber, free) meant individual freedom and equality before the law for the new middle classes. Politically it stood for government by consent, an end to autocracy and clerical privileges, a constitution and representative government, though suffrage was often limited to property-owning men. Economically it meant freedom of markets and abolition of state restrictions on goods and capital; in German lands this led to the Zollverein (1834), which abolished tariff barriers and reduced the number of currencies. These ideas strengthened demands for national unification.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.text: Explain the process of formation of 'United Kingdom of Great Britain'.
questions.solution: Britain was not formed by a sudden revolution but by a long process. Before the 18th century there was no British nation; people saw themselves as English, Welsh, Scots or Irish. The English parliament seized power from the monarchy in 1688 and became the instrument through which England extended its influence. The Act of Union (1707) between England and Scotland created the United Kingdom of Great Britain, with England dominating and Scottish culture and institutions being suppressed. Ireland, divided between Catholics and Protestants, was forcibly incorporated in 1801 after a failed revolt. The symbols of the new Britain, the Union Jack, the national anthem and the English language, were actively promoted.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: How is energy a basic requirement for economic development ? Explain.
questions.solution: Every sector needs energy: agriculture needs it for pumps, tractors and fertilisers; industry needs it to run machines; transport and communication run on it; commercial and domestic sectors use it for lighting, heating and cooking. Without enough energy, production, employment and incomes cannot grow, so energy is basic to economic development. Since consumption keeps rising, India must develop sustainable energy, using both conventional and non-conventional sources and conserving energy.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: How are conventional sources of energy different from non-conventional sources ? Explain.
questions.solution: Conventional sources (coal, petroleum, natural gas, firewood) have been used for a long time; most are exhaustible, cause pollution and are found only in certain places. Non-conventional sources (solar, wind, tidal, geothermal, biogas, nuclear) are mostly renewable, cleaner and widely available, but their use began recently and some need high initial investment and technology.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: How are democratic governments better than other forms of government ? Explain.
questions.solution: Democracy promotes equality among citizens and enhances the dignity of the individual. It improves the quality of decision-making through discussion and consultation. It provides a method to resolve conflicts peacefully. It allows room to correct mistakes. It produces an accountable, responsive and legitimate government, chosen by and answerable to the people.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: How do democracies lead to peaceful and harmonious life among citizens ? Explain.
questions.solution: No society can fully and permanently resolve conflicts among groups, but democracies handle social differences and divisions well. They respect the rule of law, allow all groups to express their views and negotiate, and give minorities a chance to share power, since majority and minority are not fixed by birth. Belgium, for example, accommodated its language groups by sharing power. This reduces the chance of tensions becoming violent and leads to a more peaceful, harmonious life.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Globalisation and the Indian Economy
questions.text: "Globalisation is the process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries." Explain the statement with examples.
questions.solution: Globalisation links countries through trade, investment, technology and people. More goods and services move across borders: Chinese toys, Indian textiles. MNCs invest in many countries and spread production, for example Ford Motors and Cargill in India, or Indian companies such as Tata buying firms abroad. Technology such as the internet allows services (IT, call centres) to be provided from far away. People also move for jobs and education. As a result, markets and production in different countries become integrated.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Globalisation and the Indian Economy
questions.text: 'Improvement in technology has stimulated the globalisation process.' Explain the statement with examples.
questions.solution: Transport technology, such as containers and faster ships and aircraft, has made delivery of goods over long distances faster and cheaper. Information and communication technology (telephones, mobiles, the internet, satellites) lets people contact one another instantly across the world. Services can be provided from far away: a magazine for London can be designed in Delhi and sent by internet, and Indian call centres serve customers abroad. MNCs can coordinate production spread across several countries.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.text:
Printed Words: This is how Mercier describes the impact of the printed word, and the power of reading in one of his books : 'Anyone who had seen me reading would have compared me to a man dying of thirst who was gulping down some fresh, pure water.... Lighting my lamp with extraordinary caution, I threw myself hungrily into the reading. An easy eloquence, effortless and animated, carried me from one page to the next without my noticing it. A clock struck off the hours in the silence of the shadows, and I heard nothing. My lamp began to run out of oil and produced only a pale light, but still I read on. I could not even take out time to raise the wick for fear of interrupting my pleasure. How those new ideas rushed into my brain! How my intelligence adopted them!'

How does the passage reflect the immersive nature of reading of Mercier ?
questions.solution: He was so absorbed that he did not notice the hours passing or the lamp running low, and would not even stop to raise the wick; he compares himself to a thirsty man gulping water.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.text:
Printed Words: Mercier describes the impact of the printed word and the power of reading : 'How those new ideas rushed into my brain! How my intelligence adopted them!'

Why did Mercier describe himself as a virtual writer ?
questions.solution: Reading made him take in and adopt the new ideas so fully that he felt he was taking part in creating them, as if he were the author himself.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.text:
Printed Words: Mercier describes the impact of the printed word and the power of reading : 'An easy eloquence, effortless and animated, carried me from one page to the next without my noticing it... How those new ideas rushed into my brain! How my intelligence adopted them!'

How did reading influence Mercier's intellectual capacity and his engagement with new concepts ? Explain in any two points.
questions.solution: Reading filled his mind with new ideas, which he eagerly absorbed and made his own. It sharpened his thinking and broadened his understanding, and it made him an enthusiastic, critical reader. Mercier believed the printing press was a powerful engine of progress, whose ideas could sweep away despotism.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Local Government: This new system of local government is the largest experiment in democracy conducted anywhere in the world. There are now about 36 lakh elected representatives in the panchayats and municipalities etc., all over the country. This number is bigger than the population of many countries in the world. Constitutional status for local government has helped to deepen democracy in our country. It has also increased women's representation and voice in our democracy. At the same time, there are many difficulties. While elections are held regularly and enthusiastically, gram sabhas are not held regularly. Most state governments have not transferred significant powers to the local governments. Nor have they given adequate resources. We are thus still a long way from realising the ideal of self-government.

Analyse the significance of the elected representatives in the Panchayats.
questions.solution: They let local people take part directly in decisions about their own area, so local problems are solved locally and democracy is deepened at the grassroots.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Local Government: Constitutional status for local government has helped to deepen democracy in our country. It has also increased women's representation and voice in our democracy.

In what way has the representation of women in democracy influenced by Constitutional status for local government ?
questions.solution: At least one-third of the seats in local bodies are reserved for women, so many more women are elected and have a voice in decision making.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Local Government: Constitutional status for local government has helped to deepen democracy in our country. At the same time, there are many difficulties. While elections are held regularly and enthusiastically, gram sabhas are not held regularly. Most state governments have not transferred significant powers to the local governments. Nor have they given adequate resources.

What has been the impact of granting Constitutional status to local government on the democratic landscape of the country ? Analyse any two impacts.
questions.solution: It made regular elections to local bodies compulsory, with State Election Commissions to conduct them, and reserved seats for SCs, STs, OBCs and women. Democracy has deepened, with about 36 lakh elected representatives and more participation by women and weaker sections. However, gram sabhas meet irregularly and states have not given enough powers and funds, so true self-government is still some way off.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Map skills (text version): (i) Name the place where Mahatma Gandhi broke salt law. (ii) Name the place where the Indian National Congress Session was held in 1927.
questions.solution: (i) Dandi (Gujarat). (ii) Madras (Chennai).
